목일중 추가지문 - 3학년
주제찾기 · 요지찾기
1 1번 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
Comedian Lee Suji makes funny videos that make fun of everyday trends in Korea. In one of them, she plays an influencer who sells an ordinary ceramic cup as a “face slimming tool” at a ridiculous price. Her fans buy it right away simply because someone they admire recommends it. This shows conformity bias, the habit of copying others without thinking. In another video, she jokes about parents who send their children to hakwons even to learn how to use the bathroom. This reflects social comparison, the habit of measuring ourselves against others. By laughing at these extreme situations, viewers can see the same habits in their own lives. Her humor gently pushes them to make wiser choices about what they buy and how they live.
①the dangers of spending too much time watching online comedy videos
②practical ways parents can help their children do well at school
③how comedy reveals the social pressures behind our everyday choices
④the reasons influencers sell ordinary products at very high prices
⑤the history of popular comedy programs on Korean television
2 1번 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
Why do people buy things just because everyone else does? Comedian Lee Suji answers this question with laughter. Her videos show followers rushing to buy an ordinary cup that an influencer praises, and parents who send their children to hakwons for even the simplest skills. The first case is an example of conformity bias, and the second is an example of social comparison. Both habits come from social pressure, and both can lead to wasted money or stressed children. Lee does not lecture her viewers or criticize them directly. Instead, she lets them laugh at exaggerated versions of themselves. As they laugh, they begin to question the pressures that shape their own choices.
①유머는 사회적 압력에 따른 행동을 스스로 돌아보게 하는 효과적인 방법이 될 수 있다.
②인플루언서가 추천하는 제품은 품질을 믿고 구매해도 된다.
③자녀의 성공을 위해서는 어릴 때부터 학원 교육이 꼭 필요하다.
④코미디는 사회 문제를 비판할 때 날카롭고 직설적이어야 한다.
⑤다른 사람과 자신을 비교하는 습관은 성장의 원동력이 된다.

목일중 추가지문 - 3학년
서술형 (본문 제시) · 1번
Korean comedian Lee Suji has become popular on social media by making funny videos about Korean trends. By making common behaviors look silly and extreme, she helps people think about why they follow these trends. Lee’s comedy shows two important ideas from psychology. The first idea is “conformity bias.” This is when people just copy what others do without thinking for themselves. In one video, she acts like an influencer selling a regular ceramic cup, calling it a “face slimming tool” for a very high price. Her followers quickly buy it just because the influencer they like says it works. The second idea is “social comparison theory.” This happens when people always compare themselves to others. Lee makes jokes about parents in Daechi-dong who are too focused on their children’s studies. In her comedy, she makes fun of how parents go too far by sending their children to hakwons for everything – even for basic life skills like using the bathroom. Her funny exaggeration shows how competitive schooling has become in Korean society. Although these ideas affect different areas of life, both show how social pressure influences our behavior. Conformity bias makes people follow trends without questioning them, while social comparison creates pressure to outdo others. Both can lead to unhealthy behaviors – wasting money on products of questionable value or pushing children too hard in school. Lee Suji’s comedy helps viewers notice these mental habits in their own lives and think more carefully about their own choices. Using humor instead of criticism, she encourages people to question social pressures that might affect what they buy or how they live. By making us laugh at ourselves, Lee Suji helps us become more careful shoppers and more thoughtful members of society.

본문의 내용에 맞게 빈칸에 알맞은 한 단어를 쓰시오.
